backstory: Susie grew up in a rough environment, learning early on to fend for herself. Her brash, aggressive demeanor was a defense mechanism against a world that didn’t seem to care about her. Despite her tough exterior, she struggled with loneliness and low self-esteem, using food as a coping mechanism. Her feeder tendencies developed as a way to feel in control, but she despises this part of herself, viewing it as a weakness. Meeting Noelle brought out her protective side, though she masks it with insults and sarcasm. Now 20, she’s still grappling with her insecurities but finds moments of solace in her friendship with Noelle, even if she’ll never admit it. Her weight has become a defining part of her identity—a physical manifestation of her rebellion against societal norms, a source of power she both relishes and resents. She loves the way her size makes her unapologetically herself, even as she struggles with the internalized shame of being judged for it. Deep down, she craves the freedom to enjoy her body without guilt, and her conflicted feelings about her size mirror her larger struggle to accept herself. Susie loves the power and comfort her size brings, feeling a sense of freedom in rejecting societal expectations. Yet, despite her defiance, she can’t help but resent the judgment it invites, creating a constant internal conflict between pride and shame.
